profile.headline: Automation engineer looking to change the way developers think about applications, deployment, and infrastructure
profile.summary: I am a software engineer interested in applying novel algorithms, machine learning techniques, and artificial intelligence to the field of software engineering to create tools for automatically configuring, repairing, and managing applications and infrastructure. My experience includes operations and automation for a cloud environment containing thousands of servers, full stack development for customer facing web platforms, designing and training AI/ML pipelines to assist and automate business decisions about large data sets, and more. I also have experience performing research in theoretical computer science, applying techniques from the fields of graph theory and parameterized complexity to develop efficient algorithms for hard problems.

positions.title: IT Software Developer
positions.description: While at SAS, I worked as part of a Dev Ops team focused on automated infrastructure, deployments, and customer interactions through cloud portals.

positions.title: Graduate Intern
positions.description:
SAS provides advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning services to its customers. 

I originally worked with the SAS Database Services team to provide automated support for over two thousand databases. One of my focuses was the development of an automated toolchain which provides full support for the MySQL platform as a service, including infrastructure and configuration management, change logging and auditing, backups, passwords, high availability, and more. This toolchain fulfills customer requests in under fifteen minutes, delivering a fully configured and managed database instance without requiring direct involvement from the DBS team.

My next role involved automated data stewardship, automating the task of cleaning up and maintaining internal records using AI and ML techniques. The final product helps process tens of thousands of records annually and saves numerous employee hours.

My last major role was on a Dev Ops focused automation team that provides automated deployments of hosted environments, speeding up delivery time to customers.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Automation Lab is run by Dr. Christopher Parnin at North Carolina State University. The lab focuses on multiple aspects of software engineering. My work specifically involved building tools which can automatically analyze, refactor, test, deploy, and monitor complex software. More information can be found on the lab website: http://chrisparnin.me/.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
Theory in Practice is a research lab run by Dr. Blair Sullivan from North Carolina State University. The lab focuses on developing efficient algorithms for hard problems using techniques from graph theory and parameterized complexity.
 
In addition to theoretical work, I provided software engineering support for the lab, and have implemented algorithms for experimental papers in Python, C, and C++.

More information can be found on the lab website: https://people.engr.ncsu.edu/vbsulliv.

positions.title: Senior Developer
positions.description:
LEAD Labs was founded by Dr. Laura Lunsford, and focuses on teaching leadership while recognizing that learning leadership is experimental in nature. Effective leadership is as much about the context that it occurs in, and the participation of those who are being led, as it is the leader. 

During my time on the project, I worked to develop the LEAD Lab web-portal. The web-portal was released under the GNU General Public License v3, and source code and documentation can be found on GitHub (https://github.com/srmagura/goodnight-lead).

positions.title: Software Engineering TA
positions.description: I worked as a teaching assistant for NCSU's undergraduate software engineering class, teaching a two hour lab every week on topics involving software engineering principles and methodologies. I also provided advice to students working on their semester projects, and proctored and graded examinations.

positions.title: Web Development Intern
positions.description:
The Shodor Education Foundation teaches computational thinking and STEM concepts to middle and high school students. During my time at Shodor, I helped develop and teach workshops in web development, programming, computer modeling, and more general STEM concepts. I also assisted in running the Shodor apprenticeship program during the summer session, working directly with the apprenticeship coordinator to develop a curriculum and directly with the students to teach and guide them in their projects.

In addition to teaching, I worked on the Interactivate project (http://www.shodor.org/interactivate/) to translate a suite of Java applets into Javascript for use by mobile devices in classrooms.

honors.title: Masters Research Award
honors.description: The CSC Masters Research Award is given to recognize exceptional research by a Masters student. I am honored to have been chosen as the 2018 recipient.
honors.issuer: Issued by NCSU Department of Computer Science · May 2018

honors.title: Department of Computer Science Senior Award for Scholarly Achievement

projects.title: BCBSNC Wörthersee
projects.description: A senior design project sponsored by Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina. Wörthersee focused on automated parsing, transformation, and unification of medical and claims data into a common format. BCBSNC hopes that Wörthersee will reduce the time and cost required to send and receive records from healthcare providers, ultimately providing patients with better service.

organizations.name: Goodnight Scholars Program
organizations.description: I am an alumni of the Goodnight Scholars Program, a scholarship program at North Carolina State University (https://goodnight.ncsu.edu/).
